name: lscpu
description: Displays detailed CPU architecture information: cores, threads, caches, frequencies, and features.

examples.output:
Architecture:            x86_64
CPU(s):                  8
  Thread(s) per core:    2
  Core(s) per socket:    4
Model name:              Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9700 CPU @ 3.00GHz
examples.explanation: 8 logical CPUs = 4 physical cores x 2 threads (hyperthreading). The real compute capacity is the core count, not the CPU(s) count.
Current and maximum CPU frequencies — useful to spot throttling.

about: lscpu collects data from /proc/cpuinfo and sysfs and presents it in a structured way. Key fields: CPU(s) (logical), Core(s) per socket x Socket(s) (physical), NUMA nodes, virtualization support, and CPU flags (look for vmx/svm for nested virtualization, avx2 for SIMD support).
useCases: Check core/thread counts for capacity planning.
Verify CPU features before installing software.
mistakes: Counting CPU(s) as physical cores — divide by Threads per core.
